name: Arrow
description: An arrow used as a melee weapon is treated as a light improvised weapon (-4 penalty on [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll))  and deals damage as a dagger of its size (critical multiplier ×2).  Arrows come in a leather quiver that holds 20 arrows. An arrow that hits  its target is destroyed; one that misses has a 50% chance of being  destroyed or lost.

name: Orc Double Axe
description: An orc double axe is a [double weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#doubleWeapons).  You can fight with it as if fighting with two weapons, but if you do,  you incur all the normal attack penalties associated with fighting with  two weapons, just as if you were using a one-handed weapon and a light  weapon.
A creature wielding an orc double axe in one hand can’t use it as a  double weapon—only one end of the weapon can be used in any given round.

name: Bolas
description: You can use this weapon to make a ranged [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attack against an opponent. You can’t be tripped during your own trip attempt when using a set of bolas.

name: Crossbow Bolt
description: A crossbow bolt used as a melee weapon is treated as a light improvised weapon (-4 penalty on [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll)) and deals damage as a dagger of its size (crit ×2). Bolts come in a wooden case that holds 10 bolts (or 5, for a [repeating crossbow](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#crossbowRepeating)). A bolt that hits its target is destroyed; one that misses has a 50% chance of being destroyed or lost.

name: Bullets, Sling
description: Bullets come in a leather pouch that holds 10 bullets. A bullet that  hits its target is destroyed; one that misses has a 50% chance of being  destroyed or lost.

name: Spiked Chain
description: A spiked chain has reach, so you can strike opponents 10 feet away with  it. In addition, unlike most other weapons with reach, it can be used  against an adjacent foe.
You can make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks with the chain. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the chain to avoid being tripped.

When using a spiked chain, you get a +2 bonus on opposed [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) made to [disarm](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#disarm) an opponent (including the roll to avoid being disarmed if such an attempt fails).

You can use the [Weapon Finesse](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/feats.htm#weaponFinesse) feat to apply your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) with a spiked chain sized for you, even though it isn’t a light weapon for you.

name: Hand Crossbow
description: You can draw a hand crossbow back by hand. Loading a hand crossbow is a [move action](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/actionsInCombat.htm#moveActions) that provokes [attacks of opportunity](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/attacksOfOpportunity.htm).

You can shoot, but not load, a hand crossbow with one hand at no  penalty. You can shoot a hand crossbow with each hand, but you take a  penalty on [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) as if attacking with two light weapons.

name: Heavy Crossbow
description: You draw a heavy crossbow back by turning a small winch. Loading a heavy crossbow is a [full-round action](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/actionsInCombat.htm#fullRoundActions) that provokes [attacks of opportunity](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/attacksOfOpportunity.htm).

Normally, operating a heavy crossbow requires two hands. However, you  can shoot, but not load, a heavy crossbow with one hand at a -4 penalty  on [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll).  You can shoot a heavy crossbow with each hand, but you take a penalty  on attack rolls as if attacking with two one-handed weapons. This  penalty is cumulative with the penalty for one-handed firing.

name: Light Crossbow
description: You draw a light crossbow back by pulling a lever. Loading a light crossbow is a [move action](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/actionsInCombat.htm#moveActions) that provokes [attacks of opportunity](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/attacksOfOpportunity.htm).

Normally, operating a light crossbow requires two hands. However, you  can shoot, but not load, a light crossbow with one hand at a -2 penalty  on [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll).  You can shoot a light crossbow with each hand, but you take a penalty  on attack rolls as if attacking with two light weapons. This penalty is  cumulative with the penalty for one-handed firing.

name: Repeating Crossbow
description: The repeating crossbow (whether heavy or light) holds 5 crossbow bolts.  As long as it holds bolts, you can reload it by pulling the reloading  lever (a [free action](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/actionsInCombat.htm#freeActions)). Loading a new case of 5 bolts is a [full-round action](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/actionsInCombat.htm#fullRoundActions) that provokes [attacks of opportunity](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/attacksOfOpportunity.htm).

You can fire a repeating crossbow with one hand or fire a repeating  crossbow in each hand in the same manner as you would a normal crossbow  of the same size. However, you must fire the weapon with two hands in  order to use the reloading lever, and you must use two hands to load a  new case of bolts.

name: Dagger
description: You get a +2 bonus on [Sleight of Hand](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/skills/sleightOfHand.htm) checks made to conceal a dagger on your body (see the [Sleight of Hand](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/skills/sleightOfHand.htm) skill).

name: Dire Flail
description: A dire flail is a [double weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#doubleWeapons).  You can fight with it as if fighting with two weapons, but if you do,  you incur all the normal attack penalties associated with fighting with  two weapons, just as if you were using a one-handed weapon and a light  weapon. A creature wielding a dire flail in one hand can’t use it as a  double weapon— only one end of the weapon can be used in any given  round.

When using a dire flail, you get a +2 bonus on opposed [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) made to [disarm](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#disarm) an enemy (including the opposed attack roll to avoid being disarmed if such an attempt fails).

You can also use this weapon to make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the dire flail to avoid being tripped.

name: Flail
description: With a flail, you get a +2 bonus on opposed [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) made to [disarm](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#disarm) an enemy (including the roll to avoid being disarmed if such an attempt fails).

You can also use this weapon to make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the flail to avoid being tripped.

name: Gauntlet
description: This metal glove lets you deal lethal damage rather than [nonlethal damage](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/injuryandDeath.htm#nonlethalDamage) with [unarmed strikes](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#unarmedStrike).  A strike with a gauntlet is otherwise considered an unarmed attack. The  cost and weight given are for a single gauntlet. Medium and heavy  armors (except breastplate) come with gauntlets.

name: Spiked Gauntlet
description: Your opponent cannot use a [disarm](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#disarm)  action to disarm you of spiked gauntlets. The cost and weight given are  for a single gauntlet. An attack with a spiked gauntlet is considered  an armed attack.

name: Glaive
description: A glaive has reach. You can strike opponents 10 feet away with it, but you can’t use it against an adjacent foe.

name: Guisarme
description: A guisarme has reach. You can strike opponents 10 feet away with it, but you can’t use it against an adjacent foe.

You can also use it to make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the guisarme to avoid being tripped.

name: Halberd
description: If you use a [ready](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialInitiativeActions.htm#ready) action to set a halberd against a [charge](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#charge), you deal double damage on a successful hit against a charging character.

You can use a halberd to make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the halberd to avoid being tripped.

name: Gnome Hooked Hammer
description: A gnome hooked hammer is a [double weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#doubleWeapons).  You can fight with it as if fighting with two weapons, but if you do,  you incur all the normal attack penalties associated with fighting with  two weapons, just as if you were using a one-handed weapon and a light  weapon. The hammer’s blunt head is a bludgeoning weapon that deals 1d6  points of damage (crit ×3). Its hook is a piercing weapon that deals 1d4  points of damage (crit ×4). You can use either head as the primary  weapon. The other head is the offhand weapon. A creature wielding a  gnome hooked hammer in one hand can’t use it as a double weapon—only one  end of the weapon can be used in any given round.

You can use a gnome hooked hammer to make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the gnome hooked hammer to avoid being tripped.
Gnomes treat gnome hooked hammers as [martial weapons](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#simpleMartialandExoticWeapons).

name: Javelin
description: Since it is not designed for melee, you are treated as [nonproficient](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatModifiers.htm#weaponArmorAndShieldProficiency) with it and take a -4 penalty on [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) if you use a javelin as a melee weapon.

name: Kama
description: The kama is a special [monk](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/classes/monk.htm) weapon. This designation gives a monk wielding a kama special options.
You can use a kama to make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the kama to avoid being tripped.

name: Lance
description: A lance deals double damage when used from the back of a charging  mount. It has reach, so you can strike opponents 10 feet away with it,  but you can’t use it against an adjacent foe.
While mounted, you can wield a lance with one hand.

name: Longbow
description: You need at least two hands to use a bow, regardless of its size. A  longbow is too unwieldy to use while you are mounted. If you have a  penalty for low Strength, apply it to damage rolls when you use a  longbow. If you have a bonus for high Strength, you can apply it to  damage rolls when you use a composite longbow (see below) but not a  regular longbow.

name: Composite Longbow
description: You need at least two hands to use a bow, regardless of its size. You  can use a composite longbow while mounted. All composite bows are made  with a particular strength rating (that is, each requires a minimum  Strength modifier to use with proficiency). If your Strength bonus is  less than the strength rating of the composite bow, you can’t  effectively use it, so you take a -2 penalty on attacks with it. The  default composite longbow requires a Strength modifier of +0 or higher  to use with proficiency. A composite longbow can be made with a high  strength rating to take advantage of an above-average Strength score;  this feature allows you to add your Strength bonus to damage, up to the  maximum bonus indicated for the bow. Each point of Strength bonus  granted by the bow adds 100 gp to its cost.
For purposes of [weapon proficiency](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatModifiers.htm#weaponArmorAndShieldProficiency) and similar feats, a composite longbow is treated as if it were a longbow.

name: Longspear
description: A longspear has reach. You can strike opponents 10 feet away with it,  but you can’t use it against an adjacent foe. If you use a [ready](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialInitiativeActions.htm#ready) action to set a longspear against a [charge](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#charge), you deal double damage on a successful hit against a charging character.

name: Net
description: A net is used to entangle enemies. When you throw a net, you make a ranged [touch attack](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#touchAttacks) against your target. A net’s maximum range is 10 feet. If you hit, the target is [entangled](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/conditionSummary.htm#entangled). An entangled creature takes a -2 penalty on [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) and a -4 penalty on Dexterity, can move at only half speed, and cannot [charge](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#charge) or [run](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/actionsInCombat.htm#run).  If you control the trailing rope by succeeding on an opposed Strength  check while holding it, the entangled creature can move only within the  limits that the rope allows. If the entangled creature attempts to cast a  spell, it must make a DC 15 [Concentration](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/skills/concentration.htm) check or be unable to cast the spell.

An entangled creature can escape with a DC 20 [Escape Artist](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/skills/escapeArtist.htm) check (a [full-round action](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/actionsInCombat.htm#fullRoundActions)). The net has 5 hit points and can be burst with a DC 25 Strength check (also a full-round action).
A net is useful only against creatures within one size category of you.

A net must be folded to be thrown effectively. The first time you throw your net in a fight, you make a normal ranged [touch attack](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#touchAttacks) roll. After the net is unfolded, you take a -4 penalty on [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) with it. It takes 2 rounds for a [proficient](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatModifiers.htm#weaponArmorAndShieldProficiency) user to fold a net and twice that long for a nonproficient one to do so.

name: Nunchaku
description: The nunchaku is a special [monk](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/classes/monk.htm) weapon. This designation gives a monk wielding a nunchaku special options. With a nunchaku, you get a +2 bonus on opposed [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) made to [disarm](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#disarm) an enemy (including the roll to avoid being disarmed if such an attempt fails).

name: Quarterstaff
description: A quarterstaff is a [double weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#doubleWeapons).  You can fight with it as if fighting with two weapons, but if you do,  you incur all the normal attack penalties associated with fighting with  two weapons, just as if you were using a one-handed weapon and a light  weapon. A creature wielding a quarterstaff in one hand can’t use it as a  double weapon—only one end of the weapon can be used in any given  round.
The quarterstaff is a special [monk](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/classes/monk.htm) weapon. This designation gives a monk wielding a quarterstaff special options.

name: Ranseur
description: A ranseur has reach. You can strike opponents 10 feet away with it, but you can’t use it against an adjacent foe.

With a ranseur, you get a +2 bonus on opposed [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) made to [disarm](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#disarm) an opponent (including the roll to avoid being disarmed if such an attempt fails).

name: Sai
description: You can use the [Weapon Finesse](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/feats.htm#weaponFinesse) feat to apply your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll)  with a rapier sized for you, even though it isn’t a light weapon for  you. You can’t wield a rapier in two hands in order to apply 1½ times  your Strength bonus to damage.

With a sai, you get a +4 bonus on opposed [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) made to [disarm](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#disarm) an enemy (including the roll to avoid being disarmed if such an attempt fails).
The sai is a special [monk](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/classes/monk.htm) weapon. This designation gives a monk wielding a sai special options.

name: Scythe
description: A scythe can be used to make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the scythe to avoid being tripped.

name: Shield Bash
description: You can bash with a shield instead of using it for defense. See Armor for details.

name: Shortbow
description: You need at least two hands to use a bow, regardless of its size. You  can use a shortbow while mounted. If you have a penalty for low  Strength, apply it to damage rolls when you use a shortbow. If you have a  bonus for high Strength, you can apply it to damage rolls when you use a  composite shortbow (see below) but not a regular shortbow.

name: Composite Shortbow
description: You need at least two hands to use a bow, regardless of its size. You  can use a composite shortbow while mounted. All composite bows are made  with a particular strength rating (that is, each requires a minimum  Strength modifier to use with proficiency). If your Strength bonus is  lower than the strength rating of the composite bow, you can’t  effectively use it, so you take a -2 penalty on attacks with it. The  default composite shortbow requires a Strength modifier of +0 or higher  to use with proficiency. A composite shortbow can be made with a high  strength rating to take advantage of an above-average Strength score;  this feature allows you to add your Strength bonus to damage, up to the  maximum bonus indicated for the bow. Each point of Strength bonus  granted by the bow adds 75 gp to its cost.

For purposes of [weapon proficiency](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatModifiers.htm#weaponArmorAndShieldProficiency) and similar feats, a composite shortbow is treated as if it were a shortbow.

name: Shortspear
description: A shortspear is small enough to wield one-handed. It may also be thrown.

name: Shuriken
description: A shuriken is a special [monk](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/classes/monk.htm) weapon. This designation gives a monk wielding shuriken special options. A shuriken can’t be used as a melee weapon.

Although they are [thrown weapons](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#thrownWeapons), shuriken are treated as [ammunition](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#ammunition) for the purposes of drawing them, crafting [masterwork](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#masterworkWeapons) or otherwise special versions of them and what happens to them after they are thrown.

name: Siangham
description: The siangham is a special [monk](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/classes/monk.htm) weapon. This designation gives a monk wielding a siangham special options.

name: Sickle
description: A sickle can be used to make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the sickle to avoid being tripped.

name: Sling
description: Your Strength modifier applies to damage rolls when you use a sling, just as it does for [thrown weapons](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#thrownWeapons). You can fire, but not load, a sling with one hand. Loading a sling is a [move action](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/actionsInCombat.htm#moveActions) that requires two hands and provokes [attacks of opportunity](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/attacksOfOpportunity.htm).

You can hurl ordinary stones with a sling, but stones are not as dense or as round as [bullets](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#bulletsSling).  Thus, such an attack deals damage as if the weapon were designed for a  creature one size category smaller than you and you take a -1 penalty on  [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll).

name: Spear
description: A spear can be thrown. If you use a [ready](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialInitiativeActions.htm#ready) action to set a spear against a [charge](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#charge), you deal double damage on a successful hit against a charging character.

name: Armor Spikes
description: You can outfit your armor with spikes, which can deal damage in a [grapple](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#grapple) or as a separate attack. See Armor for details.

name: Spiked Shield
description: You can bash with a spiked shield instead of using it for defense. See Armor for details.

name: Unarmed Strike
description: A Medium character deals 1d3 points of [nonlethal damage](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/injuryandDeath.htm#nonlethalDamage) with an unarmed strike. A Small character deals 1d2 points of nonlethal damage. A [monk](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/classes/monk.htm) or any character with the [Improved Unarmed Strike](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/feats.htm#improvedUnarmedStrike)  feat can deal lethal or nonlethal damage with unarmed strikes, at her  option. The damage from an unarmed strike is considered weapon damage  for the purposes of effects that give you a bonus on weapon damage  rolls.

An unarmed strike is always considered a light weapon. Therefore, you can use the [Weapon Finesse](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/feats.htm#weaponFinesse) feat to apply your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) with an unarmed strike.

name: Bastard Sword
description: A bastard sword is too large to use in one hand without special training; thus, it is an [exotic weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#simpleMartialandExoticWeapons). A character can use a bastard sword two-handed as a [martial weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#simpleMartialandExoticWeapons).

name: Two-Bladed Sword
description: A two-bladed sword is a [double weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#doubleWeapons).  You can fight with it as if fighting with two weapons, but if you do,  you incur all the normal attack penalties associated with fighting with  two weapons, just as if you were using a one-handed weapon and a light  weapon. A creature wielding a two-bladed sword in one hand can’t use it  as a double weapon—only one end of the weapon can be used in any given  round.

name: Trident
description: This weapon can be thrown. If you use a [ready](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialInitiativeActions.htm#ready) action to set a trident against a [charge](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#charge), you deal double damage on a successful hit against a charging character.

name: Dwarven Urgrosh
description: A dwarven urgrosh is a [double weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#doubleWeapons).  You can fight with it as if fighting with two weapons, but if you do,  you incur all the normal attack penalties associated with fighting with  two weapons, just as if you were using a one-handed weapon and a light  weapon. The urgrosh’s axe head is a slashing weapon that deals 1d8  points of damage. Its spear head is a piercing weapon that deals 1d6  points of damage. You can use either head as the primary weapon. The  other is the off-hand weapon. A creature wielding a dwarven urgrosh in  one hand can’t use it as a double weapon—only one end of the weapon can  be used in any given round.

If you use a [ready](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialInitiativeActions.htm#ready) action to set an urgrosh against a [charge](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#charge),  you deal double damage if you score a hit against a charging character.  If you use an urgrosh against a charging character, the spear head is  the part of the weapon that deals damage.
Dwarves treat dwarven urgroshes as [martial weapons](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#simpleMartialandExoticWeapons).

name: Dwarven Waraxe
description: A dwarven waraxe is too large to use in one hand without special training; thus, it is an [exotic weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#simpleMartialandExoticWeapons). A Medium character can use a dwarven waraxe two-handed as a [martial weapon](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/equipment/weapons.htm#simpleMartialandExoticWeapons),  or a Large creature can use it one-handed in the same way. A dwarf  treats a dwarven waraxe as a martial weapon even when using it in one  hand.

name: Whip
description: A whip deals [nonlethal damage](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/injuryandDeath.htm#nonlethalDamage). It deals no damage to any creature with an [armor bonus](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/theBasics.htm#armorBonus) of +1 or higher or a [natural armor bonus](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/theBasics.htm#naturalArmorBonus)  of +3 or higher. The whip is treated as a melee weapon with 15-foot  reach, though you don’t threaten the area into which you can make an  attack. In addition, unlike most other weapons with reach, you can use  it against foes anywhere within your reach (including adjacent foes).
Using a whip provokes an [attack of opportunity](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/attacksOfOpportunity.htm), just as if you had used a ranged weapon.
You can make [trip](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#trip) attacks with a whip. If you are tripped during your own trip attempt, you can drop the whip to avoid being tripped.

When using a whip, you get a +2 bonus on opposed [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) made to [disarm](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/specialAttacks.htm#disarm) an opponent (including the roll to keep from being disarmed if the attack fails).

You can use the [Weapon Finesse](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/feats.htm#weaponFinesse) feat to apply your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to [attack rolls](https://www.d20srd.org/srd/combat/combatStatistics.htm#attackRoll) with a whip sized for you, even though it isn’t a light weapon for you.
